items.headline: 川普稱停攻擊 俄烏未停手
items.context: 美國總統川普表示，俄羅斯與烏克蘭已經同意停止攻擊彼此的能源設施，背景是柴油價格持續飆漲。不過根據報導，雙方實際上仍持續對能源設施發動攻擊，這項協議能否真的落實，目前還是問號。

本則整理自 Reuters、NPR 與 Al Jazeera 於 2026 年 9 月 15 日發佈的報導。
items.threads_text:
美國總統川普宣布，俄羅斯與烏克蘭已經同意停止互相攻擊能源設施，他提出這項說法的背景，是柴油價格持續飆漲、各方都承受壓力。但根據報導，俄烏雙方實際上並沒有真的停手，能源設施攻擊仍在持續進行。這也讓人開始懷疑，川普口中的這項『協議』，究竟只是外交辭令，還是真的有落地的可能。

本則整理自 Reuters、NPR 與 Al Jazeera 於 2026 年 9 月 15 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
items.voice_text: 俄羅斯跟烏克蘭，講好要停止攻擊彼此的能源設施了嗎？至少美國總統川普是這麼說的。他提出這個說法，背景是柴油價格一直在飆漲。但實際狀況是，雙方看起來並沒有真的停手，能源設施攻擊還在持續。這項所謂的『協議』，到底是真的談成了，還是只是說說而已，目前還很難講。

本則整理自 The New York Times 與 The Guardian 於 2026 年 9 月 16 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

items.headline: 尼詠歐主演家暴新劇
items.context: 奧斯卡影后露琵塔尼詠歐（Lupita Nyong'o）在紐約 Greenwich House 劇院，主演劇作家瑪琳愛爾蘭（Marin Ireland）的作品《Pre-Existing Condition》，這部劇講述一名女性從伴侶施暴、分手後走出創傷的過程，全劇長 75 分鐘。這齣劇 2024 年首演時，就曾由塔提雅娜瑪斯蘭尼、艾迪法可等多位演員接力演出。

奧斯卡影后露琵塔尼詠歐（Lupita Nyong'o），最近在紐約 Greenwich House 劇院，主演了劇作家瑪琳愛爾蘭（Marin Ireland）的作品《Pre-Existing Condition》。劇情圍繞著一位化名『A』的女性展開，她的伴侶動手打了她，這齣戲講的就是她走出這段關係、面對創傷的過程，全長 75 分鐘。這齣劇其實 2024 年就在紐約較小的 Connelly Theater Upstairs 首演過，當時由塔提雅娜瑪斯蘭尼、艾迪法可、黛爾德麗歐康乃爾等多位演員，各自輪流演出短短幾週。這次移師到規模更大的 Greenwich House 劇院重新上演，尼詠歐打頭陣，接下來還會有菲莉帕蘇、蘇珊娜弗勒德、哈里內夫、法可再度回歸，以及惠特妮懷特輪番接棒。

sources.summary: Greenwich House Theater, New York The Oscar-winning actor transfixes in Marin Ireland’s masterfully nuanced play about a woman reeling from a toxic relationship Paradoxically, the more stars step into the lead role in Pre-Existing Condition , the more the brilliance of Marin Ireland’s domestic abuse play takes center stage. Not that it ever suffered from a lack of acting talent – when it premiered in 2024, at New York’s tiny Connelly Theater Upstairs, it counted Tatiana Maslany , Edie Falco and Deirdre O’Connell among the actors who played its central character in quick succession, for only a few weeks each. And this return engagement, at the larger Greenwich House Theater across town, kicks off with Lupita Nyong’o , before making way for Phillipa Soo, Susannah Flood, Hari Nef, Falco again and Whitney White. It’s a straightforward conceit, perfectly calibrated for a 75-minute run time. A woman (whom the script refers to as A, currently played by Nyong’o) is dealing with the aftermath of a breakup triggered by her partner hitting her. When we meet her, someone (perhaps a lawyer, or a therapist) is laying out the reality of her situation: even with the deep pockets required to go to court, it’s been seven months since the incident, it happened across state lines and she never called the police. “You have to be ready for a fight,” she tells A. “Which, just from our short time with each other, I can already tell that you’re not.” Continue reading...

sources.summary: The latest Exhibition on Screen documentary does a good job balancing the famous scandals with the subtle brilliance of his art Timed to coincide with Tate Britain’s impressive gallery show – which closes at the end of September, so you haven’t long if you’ve missed it so far – this latest from the Exhibition on Screen strand does a fine job in outlining the ins and outs, and ups and downs of this still somewhat divisive artist who, Whistler’s Mother notwithstanding, is still probably most famous for winning a farthing in damages in his “flinging a pot of paint” libel action against John Ruskin. The film assembles the customary lineup of notables including the Tate’s Carol Jacobi, critic Rachel Campbell-Johnston and art historian Stephen Calloway, the latter of whom’s dandyish attire and Colonel Sanders goatee suggests he has very much bought into the Whistler aesthetic. In fact, as all the interviewees are keen to point out, Whistler’s self-constructed persona, always with an eye to making a splash, is as significant an element of his artistic presence as the art itself – even if, as I can’t be alone in thinking, there’s something fundamentally irritating about his southern-genteel attudinising even at a century and a half’s distance. Be that as it may, the film gets to grips with Whistler’s instinctive brilliance as an artist, his natural flair for boundary-pushing and forward-thinking idealism. The big life episodes – his arrival in London, painting his mother, the brouhaha over the Peacock Room , the court case and subsequent bankruptcy – are recounted, but there is impressive detail on the actual art: from the dynamics behind his brooding Wapping picture to the temper tantrums (not his) that made Harmony in Grey and Green, his portrait of the eight-year-old Cicely Alexander so distinctive. And while Whistler’s dealings with the women in his life wouldn’t exactly pass modern-era scrutiny, his pictures of them are genuinely brilliant, with especial attention given to a wonderfully tender sketch of his wife Beatrix , terminally ill in a hotel bedroom. items.headline: 英國盼撤 波蘭擬徵暴利稅
items.context: 英國北海油氣業者呼籲政府提前 3 年（2027 年而非 2030 年）廢除對石化業者課徵的暴利稅，改用只在價格飆漲時才啟動的較窄稅制，理由是今年冬天能源帳單恐創俄烏戰爭以來新高。同一時間，波蘭則反其道而行，準備恢復對石油公司課徵暴利稅，稅收將用於補貼油價。
items.thread_text:
英國北海油氣業者呼籲政府，把對石化業者課徵的暴利稅，提前 3 年（2027 年而非原訂的 2030 年）廢除，改用只在價格飆漲時才啟動的較窄稅制，理由是今年冬天能源帳單，恐怕會創下俄烏戰爭以來的新高。同一時間，波蘭則是反其道而行，準備恢復對石油公司課徵暴利稅，稅收將用於補貼油價。

本則整理自 The Guardian 與 Reuters 於 2026 年 9 月 15 日發佈的報導。
items.threads_text:
石油暴利稅，最近在歐洲出現兩種完全相反的走向。英國北海油氣業的代表組織 Offshore Energies UK（OEUK）呼籲工黨政府，把原訂 2030 年才要撤除的暴利稅，提前 3 年、在 2027 年就廢除，改用一套範圍更窄、只在價格飆漲時才會啟動的稅制。他們的理由是，今年冬天英國的能源帳單，恐怕會創下俄羅斯入侵烏克蘭以來的新高。同一時間，波蘭卻是反過來，準備恢復對石油公司課徵暴利稅，稅收將用來補貼民眾的燃料價格，減輕物價壓力。

本則整理自 The Guardian 與 Reuters 於 2026 年 9 月 15 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
